subject: Cloud Computing
title: VMware and the Virtual Machine Boom
description: A 60-second lesson on VMware and the Virtual Machine Boom.

hook.text: In 1998, a Stanford professor and her students figured out how to virtualize Intel processors.

buildup.text: VMware made it possible to run multiple operating systems on one ordinary PC.

discovery.text: Businesses consolidated dozens of servers into a few, saving millions on hardware.

twist.text: VMware became so dominant that it controlled enterprise computing for over a decade.

climax.text: At its peak, VMware powered most data centers worldwide. Then containers arrived.

punchline.text: VMware made virtual machines mainstream. Then the game changed.

quiz.question: What was VMware's key contribution to computing?
options: Making virtualization practical on standard Intel hardware

details.summary: VMware made virtualization practical for x86 servers in the late 1990s and 2000s, allowing enterprise data centers to consolidate dozens of physical servers into fewer machines. VMware's success created the virtualization expertise and market demand that cloud providers later inherited.
details.whyItMatters: VMware brought virtualization from mainframes to commodity hardware. Without VMware making x86 virtualization mainstream, cloud computing would have lacked the technology and talent to emerge.
takeaways: VMware made x86 virtualization mainstream in enterprises
Server consolidation saved companies millions in hardware costs
VMware created the virtualization expertise cloud providers later used

faq.question: How did VMware change data centers?
faq.answer: Before VMware, each application typically ran on a dedicated physical server at low utilization. VMware let companies consolidate 10 or more servers onto one physical machine, dramatically reducing hardware, power, and cooling costs while simplifying management.

faq.question: What happened to VMware as cloud grew?
faq.answer: VMware initially competed with cloud providers but eventually partnered with them, offering VMware Cloud on AWS and similar services. Broadcom acquired VMware in 2023, raising licensing changes that pushed some customers to consider cloud-native alternatives.
